findings.expected: A wrong-root learner gets a defined partial score; the R3 F.T. clause can actually apply.
findings.actual: R1 is 'M1 identify the interior zero and signs' (JSON: 'locate root in interval and determine sign on each side'). R3 is DM1 'dependent on R1', 'with limited F.T. from a plausible visibly miscalculated interior zero'. If a miscalculated zero fails R1, R3 can never be earned, so the F.T. clause is dead. If it passes R1, the learner gets R1+R2+R3 = 3/4. The two readings differ by 2 marks for the same work.
findings.evidence: Rubric text; wrong-root sweep (split at t=c from a root sign slip) never equals the canonical distance, so only marking decides the score.
findings.repair: Define R1 as M1 for a visible attempt to solve v=0 (one slip allowed) and a sign test on each side of the learner's root in (0,T). R3 then follows through from that root.

findings.expected: The redesign's purpose (calc2-04) is that the branch needs integration. Comparable rows require an attempted primitive: E4 'both bounds in an attempted integral', R5 'attempted primitive and both bounds'.
findings.actual: R3 ('add magnitudes of both bounded legs') and R4 ('canonical total') do not require the legs to come from an attempted primitive. A learner who solves v=0, tests signs and writes calculator values for the two definite integrals earns R1+R3+R4 = 3/4 with no integration. The same route earns 0/2 on displacement, because R5 requires a primitive. Line 50 only zeroes a quadrature value with no working at all.
findings.evidence: Rubric text versus E4/R5; 2021 report PDF236: calculators that integrate are in use and answer-only work earns no marks.
findings.repair: R3: magnitudes of both legs, each evaluated from an attempted primitive with both bounds. R4: depends on R2 and R3. Alternatively, state explicitly that calculator-evaluated legs earn R1/R3 only.

findings.expected: Analyse 4 rests on a live decision. S3-04 criticised another branch because every instance had the same outcome.
findings.actual: The decision is not cued: there is no root, no rest part, and distance is asked first. But its outcome never varies. In all 108 tuples v has exactly one root in (0,T), and the other root -c is always negative, so the correct move is always 'split at the positive root'. The 54/54 'decision_outcome_classes' are only the starting direction, which leaves the method unchanged once absolute values are taken. A learner drilled on 'solve v=0, take the positive root, split' gets R1/R3 on every instance.
findings.evidence: Own enumeration: inside-root set == [r] for all 108; -c<0 always; directions 54/54.
findings.repair: Rename the field to direction classes and disclose the invariant outcome for the owner or cross-vendor decision on Analyse 4. Or admit a bounded minority with no sign change on [0,T], or a second positive root beyond T, so that whether and where to split varies.
